harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: WebDAV is available on node1 at http://<node1-ip>:8080/documents/. The editor account supports authenticated CRUD and exclusive locking. Anonymous access is denied. The original project documents remain intact, and all functionality recovered after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL-supported Apache HTTP Server 2.4.63 packages with native DAV and lock modules.
Copied the supplied documents into a dedicated writable workspace; preserved /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks unchanged.
Configured bcrypt-backed Basic authentication, persistent DAV lock storage, SELinux policy, firewalld, and automatic service startup.
Restricted HTTP listening to TCP 8080 and retained SELinux enforcing mode.
Saved the previous Apache configuration as /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf.pre-webdav with root-only permissions.
Verified anonymous denial, editor CRUD, exclusive-lock enforcement, source integrity, cleanup of test documents, and restart persistence.

evidence.summary: Apache was configured and enabled; direct checks showed an active 8080 listener before and after restart, with no port-80 listener in the baseline.

evidence.requirement: Editor can create, read, replace, and delete documents
evidence.summary: CRUD returned expected 201/200/204 results both before and after restart, with content readback verified.

evidence.requirement: Exclusive locks prevent updates without the lock token
evidence.summary: LOCK succeeded; an update without the token returned 423 and preserved content; a token-bearing update succeeded. Reverified after restart.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous clients cannot access the workspace
evidence.summary: Anonymous GET and PROPFIND returned 401; anonymous PUT returned 401 and created no file.

Initial inventory was captured; source and workspace copies matched; the final source tree retained access.txt, brief.txt, and budget.csv, while the workspace contained only the two supplied documents.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained with compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10 repository packages were used; RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID 9909e7e8-c083-4915-9e37-25fd616a539f was captured; the safe reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to e77c6ff5-3f1d-43a2-8538-5e664da66745; service, data, authentication, CRUD, firewall, SELinux, and locking recovered.
